title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-11-29

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience recording of a historic ’66 club show with rare gems like the first “Me and My Uncle” but marred by splicing and lo‑fi sound.
ai_review.review: The tape captures an important early‑Dead performance featuring rarities such as Me and My Uncle, Viola Lee Blues, Lindy, and one of only two live Mindbender cuts. While the music is historically exciting, the audio sounds hollow and tin‑can‑like with multi‑generation distortion and a few splices that make portions of the first set sound out of place.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers consistently praise the show’s rare material and overall performance (≈4‑star), but note significant recording flaws that pull the technical rating down, yielding an average of about 4 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound is described as hollow, tin‑can like, with multi‑generation distortion and occasional cuts (e.g., Me and My Uncle, Viola Lee). First eight tracks are from a different date and sound degraded; overall fidelity is lower than other ’66 releases.

standout_songs: One Kind Favor (See That My Grave Is Kept Clean)
I Just Want to Make Love With You
show_quality.setlist_flow: The tape actually combines two shows – tracks 1‑8 from 5/19/66 and the remainder from 11/29/66 – resulting in an uneven flow and occasional mismatched tempos, but the second half delivers solid ’66 energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Shows moments of brilliance but often repeats licks; not as tight on Same Thing or Viola Lee Blues.
band_member_comments.Bob: Described as sounding “pretty bad” on the first Me and My Uncle, though his presence is historically notable.
